title: SMBv1 server protocol is enabled
description: [DEMO DATA - not from a real system] The SMB 1.0 server component is enabled. SMBv1 lacks modern integrity and encryption protections and is deprecated by Microsoft.
impact: SMBv1 has been used by wormable malware (e.g. WannaCry via MS17-010). If a related patch is missing, remote code execution may be possible.
references: CVE-2017-0144 (CVSS v3.1 8.1, NVD (sample reference)); MS-SecBaseline: Configure SMB v1 server = Disabled (Microsoft Security Baseline)
remediation: Disable SMBv1 after confirming no legacy clients depend on it: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol (run by an administrator during a change window, not by this tool).
verification: Get-SmbServerConfiguration | Select EnableSMB1Protocol should return False.
severity_rationale: High: configuration directly observed and network-exposed; not Critical because MS17-010 patch status is assessed separately.

title: SSH permits direct root login with a password
description: [DEMO DATA - not from a real system] The effective sshd configuration has PermitRootLogin yes and PasswordAuthentication yes.
impact: Attackers can target the root account directly with password guessing; a successful guess grants full control and bypasses per-user accountability.
evidence_summary:
Effective sshd settings (sample) [sshd -T] permitrootlogin yes
passwordauthentication yes
references: CIS Ubuntu Linux: Ensure sshd PermitRootLogin is disabled (CIS Benchmark (title only; content licensed separately))
remediation: Set 'PermitRootLogin no' (or 'prohibit-password') and 'PasswordAuthentication no' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/, then reload sshd.
severity_rationale: High: directly observed, remotely reachable, targets the most privileged account.

title: Remote Desktop allows connections without Network Level Authentication
description: [DEMO DATA - not from a real system] RDP is enabled and UserAuthentication = 0, so the logon screen is presented before the client authenticates.
impact: Unauthenticated users can reach the logon screen, increasing exposure to brute-force attempts and pre-authentication vulnerabilities.
remediation: Require NLA via Group Policy: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Remote Desktop Services > Security > 'Require user authentication for remote connections by using NLA' = Enabled.
verification: reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp" /v UserAuthentication should show 0x1.
severity_rationale: Medium: weakens an authentication control on a remote service; not High because RDP exposure is limited to the internal network.

title: Security updates are pending for 3 packages
description: [DEMO DATA - not from a real system] apt reports upgradable packages from the -security pocket. The installed versions may be vulnerable to the issues fixed by these updates.
impact: Unpatched packages may contain exploitable vulnerabilities.
remediation: Apply updates during a maintenance window: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade.
verification: apt list --upgradable 2>/dev/null | grep -- -security should return nothing.
severity_rationale: Medium/potential: based on package metadata only; individual CVE applicability and exploitability were not confirmed.

title: System volume encryption status could not be determined
description: [DEMO DATA - not from a real system] No LUKS mapping was found for the root filesystem, but the volume may be protected by hardware (SED) or hypervisor-level encryption.
impact: If the disk is unencrypted, data could be read from a stolen or decommissioned drive.
remediation: Confirm the encryption approach with the platform owner; enable LUKS or equivalent where policy requires encryption at rest.
verification: lsblk -o NAME,TYPE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT and the hypervisor/storage console.
severity_rationale: Low/inconclusive: absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.
